History & Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Adult male with 5-day history of dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias, mild throat irritation—no dyspnea or systemic red flags—consistent with viral upper respiratory tract infection; advised supportive care and return precautions.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Dry “hacking” cough and common-cold symptoms.  
• Onset/duration: Began ~5 days ago (start of last weekend); unchanged since onset.  
• Characteristics/progression:
  – Dry cough, no sputum, no hemoptysis.  
  – Runny nose, muscle aches, intermittent headache, chills.  
  – Denies shortness of breath, wheeze, or chest tightness.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Takes paracetamol with partial relief; no NSAID use.  
• Associated symptoms: None reported beyond above; denies neck gland swelling.  
• Review of systems: Respiratory negative for dyspnea/wheeze; Cardiovascular negative for palpitations/chest pain; Endocrine—home blood sugars unchanged.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus × ~5–6 yrs; self-monitors glucose, currently stable.  
• Hypertension (“slight”); reports recent BP within normal range.  
• No complications reported.

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Paracetamol (acetaminophen) PRN for symptoms – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
• Smoking: not discussed.  
• Alcohol/substance use: not discussed.  
• Other: No relevant social factors stated.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
Vitals: Not provided.  
HEENT: Mild erythema of posterior pharynx; tonsils not enlarged. No palpable cervical lymphadenopathy (per patient self-exam).  
Chest: No wheeze or breathlessness reported; no auscultation performed.  
Cardiovascular/Abdominal/Neuro: Not examined.

Investigations:
None.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold)  
  – No evidence of bacterial infection or lower respiratory involvement.  
  – Plan:
    • Symptomatic relief: Over-the-counter preparations (Day Nurse/Night Nurse) compatible with current meds.  
    • Continue paracetamol as needed.  
    • Maintain hydration and rest.  
    • Red-flag advice: Seek medical review if new shortness of breath, wheeze, chest pain, haemoptysis, fever >3 weeks, or general deterioration.  

Issue 2: Chronic conditions (Type 2 DM, HTN) – stable  
  – Plan:
    • Continue current medications as prescribed.  
    • Continue home monitoring of blood glucose and blood pressure.  
    • Routine follow-up with primary care per usual schedule.

General Plan Items:
• No prescription required today.  
• Return consult if any concerns or if condition fails to improve within expected timeframe.
